messages:
harper: seeing a weird spike of 403s for on-prem admin console access in tenant 'acme-corp' after the RBAC refactor PR-492 landed. anyone else? :thinking_face:
maria: yep saw a paging alert. happens when they try to open the controlplane UI, also CLI `redwoodctl get deployments` returns 403 with `permission denied`
dmitri: logs show KMS unwrap failures around the same time for the same principal: `AccessDenied: kms:Decrypt denied for key arn:aws:kms:.../rw-cmk-01`
maria: that's odd — the role bindings we shipped included `allow_network_scoped: true` to narrow admin perms by VPC allowlist. I wonder if the new role-inheritance filter is dropping the `cloudkms:Decrypt` permission from the effective policy when network_scope is set
harper: can you paste the binding?
maria: sure — here's the binding from tenant config: ```json
{
  "subject": "group:acme-admins",
  "roles": ["private_admin"],
  "conditions": {"network_scope": "vpc-tenant-acme"}
}
```
dmitri: and our role definition for private_admin includes `kms:Decrypt` via `service-svcprincipal` role mapping. The refactor added an optimization that prunes permissions not explicitly allowed by the network_scope. Looks like `kms` permissions are considered global and got filtered out.
harper: ugh. so ephemeral session token can't unwrap keys -> 403s. Impact: on-prem admins can't manage private control plane for that tenant. Need rollback or hotfix.
maria: quick mitigation: remove the `network_scope` condition on the binding for acme-admins, that'll immediately restore effective perms. But we should be cautious — that widens the admin scope temporarily.
dmitri: I can push a temporary allowlist change. Running: `rbacctl update-binding --subject group:acme-admins --remove-condition network_scope` — will do if @harper ok
harper: do it, but also create a short-lived audit entry and tag the change as emergency-rollback. add KMS audit reason.
dmitri: running now. response: `OK binding updated (rc=0)`. admins report controlplane access restored.
sec-bot: automated-audit: change detected by dmitri: removed condition network_scope from binding group:acme-admins. Ticket created: SEC-8721.
maria: next steps: revert the pruning optimization in PR-492 and add explicit whitelist for KMS permissions to survive network-scoped filtering. Also add an integration test that simulates KMS unwrap flow with network-scoped bindings.
harper: agree. assign to PR-492 author (samir) for hotfix revert. samir oncall? @samir ?
harper: sampler: tagging for visibility — we need a patch that ensures permissions required for control plane operations (kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, secrets:Get) are always preserved even when network_scope condition is present (unless explicitly denied). Also update docs about interaction between network-scoped bindings and global service permissions.
maria: I'll draft the test and a minimal policy patch. dmitri can keep the temporary binding change until the patch lands and is rolled.
dmitri: will notify infra-runbook and extend monitoring for similar 403/KMS errors across tenants for the next 24h.
harper: thanks. add postmortem note in SEC-8721: impact, mitigation, root cause (pruning optimization removed required KMS grants when network-scoped condition existed), and follow-ups (test, doc, revert+patch).
maria: quick note — we should also scan dedicated clusters where onprem KMS keys are customer-managed, to ensure we don't have asymmetric KMS policies that would still block unwrap even after RBAC fix.
harper: good call. dmitri can you add that to the ticket?
dmitri: yep added. SEC-8721 updated. closing this thread. :white_check_mark:
